text:
sarah: FYI — Acme opened an escalation: they saw a latency spike + unexpected billing increase yesterday and attached a red-team finding that claims KMS alias metadata was exposed. Escalating to eng-security/infra to triage.
acme-cs: ""We saw a 3x latency increase from ~13:30-14:10 UTC and a billing jump on the same window. Red team sent a note that DescribeKey calls returned alias names for some prefixes — they think it could be used to enumerate key names. We can share the red-team report if needed.""
jess: Can you drop the red-team report link and the exact timestamps/request ids? Need specific repro steps to validate. Also, any CloudTrail S3 link would help.
sarah: attaching excerpt (redacted):
```
2026-03-16T13:42:07Z DescribeKey arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-1234 alias/rnw-prod-analytics
2026-03-16T13:42:08Z DescribeKey arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/efgh-5678 alias/rnw-prod-encoder
```
They included a suggested repro: iterative DescribeKey calls against a range of alias prefixes, ~100k calls over ~30m from a handful of IPs.
raj: If true this would be high-volume DescribeKey traffic. Two fronts: 1) security (can aliases be enumerated via DescribeKey?) and 2) ops/billing (why did token usage spike). Can someone paste the CloudTrail query results for that window?
mike: Also worth checking if we had a key rotation job running during that window — rotation can spike KMS RPCs and cause retries. I'll pull HSM logs.
audit-bot: New incident ticket created: INC-4512. CloudTrail archive: s3://redwood-ct-archives/prod/2026/03/16/ct-2026-03-16-13.gz (access restricted).
jess: Initial take: likely low-severity if only alias names were visible and no plaintext data was exfil'd, but medium if the finding allows downstream discovery of customer-specific keys. We should confirm whether DescribeKey returned alias metadata for keys outside of the requester's account and whether IAM policies allowed those calls.
sarah: Red-team supplied repro steps (redacted):
```bash
for p in {0000..ffff}; do
  aws --region us-west-2 kms describe-key --key-id alias/rnw-prod-$p || true
done
```
They said the loop produced 3–4 matching alias names per 10k attempts.
raj: Quick cluster check: I ran a query on request logs and saw ~29k DescribeKey calls between 13:35 and 14:05 UTC from IPs tagged as red-team. Sample: requestId=xyz-1234-req, principal=redteam@partners, sourceIp=3.120.45.200. Those calls mostly returned 403 or 404, but ~120 returned 200 with alias names. Posting small query output: 
```
count(*) where eventName='DescribeKey' and eventTime between '2026-03-16T13:30:00Z' and '2026-03-16T14:10:00Z' -> 29,432
```
mike: HSM note: we performed scheduled HSM rotation for the 'rnw-prod' cluster at 2026-03-16T13:50:12Z. Rotation completed successfully. During rotation we saw an uptick in KMS RPC latency and some retries from the serving fleet which could explain customer-facing latency. No export operations recorded in HSM logs.
jess: OK that helps. Two parallel tracks: reproduce the red-team enumeration in a controlled staging environment to confirm the exact behavior, and produce evidence that key material was never exported. We also need to determine whether DescribeKey should be returning alias metadata for principals that shouldn't see them — that might be an IAM policy issue.
sarah: Customer wants an itemized billing breakdown and proof no secret material was leaked. I'll prepare a response but need final data for the billing window and a signed statement about HSM/export.
raj: I'll run a billing reconciliation: compare KMS API call counts vs token-metered billing for that timeframe and look for anomalies (e.g., double-counted tokens due to retries).
mike: Quick metrics snippet from the serving fleet (13:30–14:10 UTC):
```
avg_kms_latency_ms: baseline=18ms -> peak=210ms
retries_per_min: baseline=0.2 -> peak=3.8
```
Retries likely increased token consumption and client-side timeouts.
jess: For the security retest plan:
- Reproduce enumeration in staging with the same call pattern
- Capture CloudTrail, KMS service logs, HSM audit logs and serving-side traces
- Confirm alias visibility semantics under different IAM principals
- Produce a signed audit note confirming no key material export
Who can run the replay? @mike?
mike: I can run the staging replay tomorrow 2026-03-17 18:00 UTC. I'll throttle to match red-team cadence and capture full logs, then anonymize ARNs in artifacts.
raj: I'll finish the billing reconciliation by EOD tomorrow and link a cost breakdown. If retries caused token doubling, we should offer a credit.
sarah: I'll draft the customer reply: ETA for retest artifacts and an interim mitigation: 1) temporarily restrict DescribeKey to admin principals, 2) rotate any aliases we think are exposed, 3) issue provisional billing credit for the spike pending reconciliation. :slightly_smiling_face:
jess: Sounds good. If retest confirms enumeration is due to permissive IAM, severity stays medium and we fix policies. If we see evidence of cross-account metadata disclosure or HSM export attempts, escalate to high and open a P0. :eyes:
acme-cs: Appreciate the quick triage. Please include the timeline and any logs we can review; they want assurance this didn't expose customer data.
sarah: Will do — I'll send a timeline + next steps by EOD. Assigning follow-ups: retest -> mike, billing reconciliation -> raj, security evidence + signed audit -> jess. Posting reaction :thumbsup:
jess: I'll prepare a short postmortem template if we need it after retest. Thanks all.
